la:adj:anxius.html:
anxĭus, a, um, adj.
v. ango
,
distressed, solicitous, uneasy, troubled, anxious (as a permanent state of mind).
Lit.: neque omnes anxii, qui anguntur aliquando, nec qui anxii semper anguntur,; cf.: anxietas and angor.—But frequently momentary' anxiae aegritudines et acerbae,: anxio animo aut sollicito esse,: spiritus anxius,: senes morosi et anxii,: Oratio pauperis, cum anxius fuerit,: anxius curis,: mentes, * : anxius angor,; : anxium habere aliquem, to bring one into trouble, to make anxious or solicitous, Auct. B. Afr. 71; .—With gen. animi or mentis: animi anxius, Cort., where Dietsch reads animo, and Gerl. omits it altogether: anxius mentis, (for this gen. v. animus, II. B. 1.).—The object on account of which one is anxious or solicitous is put,
In abl.: gloriā ejus,: omine adverso,: venturis,.—
In gen. (diff. from

the preced. gen. animi and mentis): inopiae,: furti (i. e. ne furtum fiat),: vitae,: securitatis,: potentiae,: sui,; in acc. vicem, .—

With de: de famā ingenii,: de successore,: de instantibus curis,; with pro, .—
With ad: ad eventum alicujus rei,.—(ε) With in and abl.: noli anxius esse in divitiis,.—(ζ) With ne and an: anxius, ne bellum oriatur,: anxius, an obsequium senatūs an studia plebis reperiret,.—
Transf.
In an act. sense, that makes anxious, troubles, awakens solicitude, troublesome: curae, (cf.: anxius curis,): timor,: accessu propter aculeos anxio,.—
Prepared with anxious care: elegantia orationis neque morosa neque anxia,; cf. anxietas, II.—Hence, adv.: anxĭē, anxiously, with anxiety (not in Cic.): aliquid ferre,: auguria quaerere,: certare,: aliquam prosequi, Justin. 1, 4: loqui,: anxie doctus,; .—Comp.: anxius, Gargil. Mai; and formed by magis: magis anxie,

la:noun:anxitudo.html:
anxĭtūdo, ĭnis, f. (mostly ante-class.), and anxĭĕtūdo, ĭnis, f. (post-class. for the class. anxietas) [id.],
anxiety, trouble, anguish: animi, Pac. ap. ; ; .—Once also in Cic.: anxitudo prona ad luctum, Rep. 2, 41: macerabatur anxietudine,: anxietudinis poena,.

la:verb:anxio.gloss: to make uneasy or anxious, worry
senses: to make uneasy or anxious, worry
la:verb:anxio.html:
anxĭo, āre, v. a.
anxius
,
to make uneasy or anxious (only in late Lat.): anxiatum iri,: dum anxiaretur cor meum,: anxiatus est super me spiritus,.

la:noun:anxietas.html:
anxĭĕtas, ātis, f.
anxius
.
The quality or state of anxius, anxiety (as a per manent condition, while angor, anguish, is only momentary; cf. Hab. Syn. 108, and v. angor),: perpetua anxie tas,.—But sometimes = angor, temporary anguish, fear, trouble, etc.: animi,; : divortii anxietate mortuus,.—
Anxious care, carefulness in regard to a thing (only post-Aug.): quaerendi, judicandi, comparandi anxietas, Quint. prooem. 8 fin.: anxietas et quasi morositas disputationis,; cf. anxius, B.

la:adj:anxifer.html:
anxĭfer, fĕra, fĕrum, adj.
anxius-fero
,
causing or bringing anxiety (only in Cic.): curae,: dolorum vertices,.
